messages:
dina: Hey team, spotted something odd in the audit stream — analytics-svc-account appears to have successfully Decrypt on cust-prod-cmk at 03:12 UTC. Not expected for analytics.
ben: Can you paste the log line? We need principal, key id, and request metadata.
dina: Sure — cloudtrail snippet: `eventTime=2026-03-19T03:12:14Z userIdentity.principalId=serviceAccount:analytics-svc-account@redwood.iam.amazonaws.com eventName=Decrypt resources=[arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cust-prod-cmk]`.
alice: ugh. That SA should only have read on metrics bucket, no kms:Decrypt. Did we just finish the rbac refactor on namespaces yesterday?
chun: We merged the cross-namespace-binding change at ~00:30 UTC. It added a ClusterRoleBinding that accidentally referenced `analytics-viewer` but pointed to `analytics-svc-account` and wildcarded the subject namespace.
ben: That sounds like a crossbind cascade — cluster-level binding granting extra privileges down the chain.
dina: Confirmed: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding crossbind-analytics -o yaml` shows `subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: analytics-svc-account
    namespace: *` (the refactor script expanded to all namespaces).
alice: Immediate mitigation: remove the offending ClusterRoleBinding or restrict it. If we remove it we restore least-privilege quickly.
chun: Agreed. We should also apply a short-lived policy to deny kms:Decrypt for analytics-svc-account while we triage. Faster to throttle impact.
sec-bot: ALERT: KMS Decrypt matched rule KMS-SUSPICIOUS-ACCESS for key cust-prod-cmk — 1 match. Created incident INC-2026-138.
oncall: I'll take oncall. Dina, can you run the quick commands to list active bindings and revoke?
dina: Running now:
```
# list and confirm
kubectl get clusterrolebinding crossbind-analytics -o yaml
# remove
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding crossbind-analytics
# verify
kubectl auth can-i decrypt --as system:serviceaccount:analytics:analytics-svc-account --namespace=prod
```
Done the delete at 03:20 UTC. `kubectl auth can-i` now returns `no` for decrypt.
ben: Good. Chun, can you push a short deny policy to IAM to be extra-safe? Something like:
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cust-prod-cmk",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/analytics-svc-role"}
    }
  ]
}
```
chun: I'm applying a conditional deny with a 1-hour expiry via org policy push. Will post policy id shortly.
ben: We should also audit what data was accessed. Dina, can you query S3 access logs and Athena for any GetObject calls by that SA in last 24h?
dina: Running quick S3 query now. Early result: 8 GetObject on `s3://customer-prod-data/` between 02:50-03:15 UTC. Files look like aggregated metrics tarballs, not plaintext PII, but still sensitive.
alice: Next actions: 1) Keep deny in place until we finish root cause. 2) Roll back refactor PR to avoid reintroducing. 3) Rotate CMK if we detect misuse beyond expected. 4) Postmortem and notify affected customers if needed.
chun: PR rollback prepared: `revert: deny-explicit-crossbind-refactor` will be merged in 10m. I'm also adding stricter subject namespace checks in the refactor script.
ben: Forensics checklist: CloudTrail full trace for the Decrypt, S3 object access, any data exfil attempts, and whether any downstream service read the decrypted plaintext. Also check Vault/KMS key policy changes timeline.
oncall: I'll take ownership of the incident until resolved. Assigning to @dina for triage, @chun for patch/rollback, @ben for forensics, @alice for customer comms.
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-138 updated: status=mitigated controls=clusterrolebinding_deleted, iam_deny_applied.
alice: We'll run a brief customer impact assessment; initial impression: low risk but need to be transparent. I'll draft a short notice for the CS/Account teams.
dina: Quick note: no evidence yet of decryption being used to exfiltrate raw keys. Still scraping logs and will update in 30m.
ben: Excellent work fast. After this, let's add a CI guard on the refactor script (reject wildcard namespace expansion) and add an integra test that verifies serviceaccounts don't gain KMS decrypt.
chun: Adding both to the backlog and will include a pre-merge hook.
alice: Thanks, team. We'll reconvene in 45m for a status update.
